title: Realize a supplied localized polynomial algebra map as a scheme chart
statement: Let X and T be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and f : X → T locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Put A = Γ(T, O_T), B = Γ(X, O_X), and equip B with an A-algebra structure whose structure map is the map on sections of f. Let g be an element of B, n a natural number, and φ : A[t_1,...,t_n] → B[1/g] an A-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Suppose this map is of finite type and is quasi-finite at every prime of B[1/g] [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then there is a locally finitely presented, Mathlib-locally-quasi-finite morphism e : D(g) → A^n_T [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] whose composite with projection is D(g).ι followed by f. Here D(g) is the fixed basic open of X; no point or dimension hypothesis is made.

source.place: Tag 00QE conclusion, used in the first reduction of the proof of Tag 00RH; principal open identification Tag 00E4. Finite presentation is the affine criterion in Mathlib and RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_comp_finiteType.

proof.text: Set U=D(g). Mathlib isLocalization_away_of_isAffine identifies Γ(X,U) as a localization of B away from g, and IsLocalization.algEquiv supplies the canonical B-algebra equivalence E from B[1/g]. Rename ULift(Fin n) to Fin n by MvPolynomial.renameEquiv. Compose its ring homomorphism with φ and E, obtaining ψ. Define e as U.isoSpec.hom, followed by Spec(ψ), followed by the inverse affine-space isomorphism. All data is explicitly constructed.

For every base prime p, quasi-finiteness at each q over p says that every corresponding singleton in Spec(κ(p) tensor_A B[1/g]) is open. The fibre spectrum is thus discrete and, as a spectrum, compact, hence finite. PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber transfers finiteness to each contraction fibre. Algebra.QuasiFinite.iff_finite_comap_preimage_singleton gives RingHom.QuasiFinite φ. Compose with the two ring equivalences and apply the affine quasi-finiteness criterion. Scheme isomorphisms preserve local quasi-finiteness, giving it for e. This argument is the proved private helper quasiFinite_of_primewise.

The structure map A→B is finitely presented by f.finitePresentation_appTop. A principal localization B→B[1/g] is finitely presented, hence so is their composite. Algebra compatibility identifies that composite with φ composed with the constants inclusion A→A[t]. The latter inclusion is finite type; RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_comp_finiteType yields finite presentation of φ. Composing with the two ring equivalences and applying LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff gives local finite presentation of e.

The constants commute with the variable-renaming equivalence, φ and E. Thus ψ composed with C is the restriction of f.appTop to U. Applying Spec, AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_inv_over, Scheme.isoSpec_inv_naturality and IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_toSpecΓ proves e followed by the affine-space projection equals U.ι followed by f. This also works when g=0 or n=0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_chart_of_localized_polynomial_map
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine T]
    (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    [Algebra Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)]
    (halg : algebraMap Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) = f.appTop.hom)
    (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) (n : ℕ)
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(T, ⊤) →ₐ[Γ(T, ⊤)] Localization.Away g)
    (hft : @Algebra.FiniteType (MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(T, ⊤)) (Localization.Away g)
      _ _ φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra)
    (hq : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away g),
      @Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime (MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(T, ⊤)) (Localization.Away g)
        _ _ φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra hft q) :
    ∃ e : (X.basicOpen g).toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T,
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation e ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite e ∧
      e ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T ↘ T) = (X.basicOpen g).ι ≫ f
